description: PLAN ONLY (no implementation yet): an agent-led robot research loop. The north-star outcome: a model we can put any task in front of, and it just works on the task until it's done. How we get there is open. Setup to plan: a strong LLM agent leads the research (with Jake's input) and has (a) exact joint-level control of the SO-101 arms and our hand, (b) rented GPUs, (c) lots of data, (d) an open generalist starting model (MolmoAct2 first, per the plans). The agent can request whatever it needs: Jake or other humans recording demonstrations (filed as human-lane pebbles, e.g. 'record 20 demos of the cup pick'), its own scripted motions, autonomous practice, sim, training runs. The core requirement is that improvement is VERIFIABLE. Plan the scoreboard first: a held-out task suite never trained on, fixed reset start states, automatic camera-judged pass/fail, enough trials per round to separate real gains from noise, and success-rate trend tracking. Cover: auto-reset fixtures, data-request workflow, compute budget, safety/hardware wear, the human-mirror setup (two eye-height stereo cameras), and a first narrow milestone that proves the loop climbs. Output: plans/agent_led_research.md, for Jake to review before anything is built.

results.identified_issue: Trial counts come from a Wilson interval and an exact McNemar sample-size estimate, assuming 30% of start states give discordant results. The first gate should measure the real rate and the counts should be recomputed from it. Prices are the RunPod figures from robot_model_scouting.md. The H100 price, LoRA run duration, the STS3215 temperature threshold, and whether a scripted cube grasp resets reliably are all unverified, and the doc says so. Main design choices: (1) hide the exam suite from the agent to stop it overfitting the leaderboard; (2) code-based judge over a VLM judge, because a VLM judge is noisier and easier to game; (3) paired, interleaved, incumbent-rerun gates so rig drift doesn't masquerade as progress; (4) narrow milestone on a cube rather than paper, so the first test is of the loop and not of Hand 1.0. A real risk: MolmoAct2 SO-101 was trained on top+side views, and eye-height stereo may score near zero zero-shot. The plan lets the agent ask for a temporary diagnostic top camera, but that is Jake's call.
results.summary: Wrote the plan in plans/agent_led_research.md. Nothing is built. The core of it is a scoreboard the research agent cannot edit. There are two suites: a dev suite the agent iterates on, and an exam suite you write privately. The agent never sees exam videos, and exam objects, spots and wordings are banned from training data. Every trial starts from a fixed start state, and an overhead camera that the model never sees scores pass or fail with code, not a language model. That judge only counts once it agrees with your hand labels on at least 95% of 100 trials. The current 5 trials per task can't tell models apart (3/5 means anywhere from 23% to 88%). Instead, a candidate and the current best each run the same 50 exam start states, interleaved, and the candidate is promoted only if an exact paired test gives p < 0.05. That reliably detects a gain of about 20 points; smaller gains are reported as not shown. The headline number is held-out success within a time budget with retries allowed, because 'works on it until it's done' needs a done-check and retry loop on top of the policy. The plan also covers auto-reset (a scripted cube grasp, a funnel bowl that returns the cube, mat walls), data requests filed as human-lane pebbles that each name the failure they target and a predicted gain, default caps of $50 a week of compute and 2 hours a week of your time, a power-cut e-stop plus servo temperature and stall monitoring, and the same stereo pair on a head strap and a pinned robot mast. The first milestone is cube into bowl with one arm and the stock jaw: beat zero-shot MolmoAct2 on unseen spots and an unseen object, for at most $150 and 6 hours of your time. Five questions for you are at the end of the doc, starting with whether 'success with retries within a time budget' is the right headline number.
results.detailed_description: New file: plans/agent_led_research.md (§1 scoreboard: dev and exam suites, start states, camera judge, trial-count tables, ledger and manifest; §2 the loop and a supervisor for retries until done; §3 auto-reset; §4 data requests; §5 compute; §6 safety and wear; §7 human-mirror cameras; §8 first milestone; §9 after it; decisions for Jake; unverified assumptions). It builds on the existing robot_eval/ harness and tasks.json and does not replace them. Changes beyond what was asked: the plan proposes an overhead judge-only camera, which I read as allowed under the human-mirror rule because the policy never sees it (question 2). It also says the existing 5-trials-per-task protocol in robot_eval is statistically too weak.

user_request.name: The AI is leading the research, with some of my input, and it can get whatever it needs: me or other humans running tons of demonstrations, or controlling the arm itself. The key is that it's verifiable that it's improving. It's just a plan for now. The fundamental thing is I don't care how it happens, but we need to end up with a model where we can set a task in front of it and it will just work on the task and get it done.

summary: Jake wants a plan document, plans/agent_led_research.md, for an LLM-agent-led research loop on SO-101 arms starting from MolmoAct2, covering fixtures, data requests, compute, safety, and cameras. The scoreboard comes first: a held-out task suite with fixed resets, camera-judged pass/fail, and enough trials to separate real gains from noise, plus a narrow first milestone proving the loop climbs.
